title: 第19章 天赋灵材
novel_title: 我有一个黑暗密武世界
content_zh:
小卖部门口。

    陈峰盯着雾中那块歪斜的匾额，心跳微微加速。

    期待了这么久，终于能进去看看了。

    他握紧斩刀，朝武馆方向摸了过去。

    到门口先停住，没有急着进去。

    而是先弯腰捡了几块碎石，朝武馆大门里扔了进去。

    石头落地，弹跳了几下，声音在空旷的室内回荡。

    没有任何回应。

    他又等了十几秒，确认里面没有其他异种生物的动静，这才侧身闪进门内。

    武馆一楼的大厅很宽敞，少说有两百平，但此时已经面目全非。

    地面上铺满了灰白色的蛛丝残网，角落里堆着碎骨头和不明残骸。

    几根承重柱上也缠着厚厚的丝线，粘连着碎布片和发霉的木板。

    空气里弥漫着一股酸腐味，混合着蛛类特有的腥臭。

    这里已经被猎影蛛改造成了巢穴。

    陈峰皱了皱眉，小心翼翼地踩着蛛丝往里走。

    墙壁上倒是还残留着一些东西。

    蛛丝下面，隐约能看到裱框的照片和文字介绍。

    陈峰用刀背拨开覆盖的丝网，露出下面的内容。

    一张泛黄的照片，照片里是一个健硕的中年男人，赤着上身，摆着一个奇怪的架势。

    脊背弯曲，双臂下垂，整个人的姿态弯折扭曲，不像人，倒像是一条立起来的胖蛇。

    照片下面有一行小字：

    “蛇脊流第六十四代传人——刘长河。”

    “省二级武师，东海市武术协会会员。”

    旁边还有有几面墙上还贴着大幅的宣传海报。

    “蛇脊流——以柔克刚，以巧胜拙。”

    “刘氏武馆，建馆十七年，培养弟子二百余人。”

    ……

    陈峰一面走一面看。

    蛇脊流的核心理念，是模拟蛇类脊椎的运动方式，进行修行和搏杀。

    并通过特殊的法门和密药，逐步打开人体的基因锁，从而实现身体素质的跨越式提升。

    这些信息和日记里记载的基本吻合……

    随后，陈峰在一楼翻了一圈，但却并没有找到任何功法典籍或者教学手稿之类的东西。

    接着又上二楼的馆主办公室，也详细的找了一遍。

    柜子都是打开的，抽屉全部散落在地上，里面空空如也。

    剩余的一些散落的泛黄文件，也大多都是是学员登记表和收费记录，没什么用。

    “功法呢……”

    陈峰站起来，皱着眉扫视四周。

    按理说，一间武馆，功法秘籍这种最核心的东西，应该就放在馆主办公室才对。

    如果连这里都没有的话，那大概率意味着其他地方也没有了……

    陈峰心头涌起一阵不甘。

    “不至于吧……”

    费了这么大的劲儿，居然什么都没找到？

    “我不信。”

    他走出馆主办公室，又往走廊深处继续走去。

    后面的几个房间，似乎都是宿舍，门牌上写着“学员宿舍1号”、“学员宿舍2号”……一路排到六号。

    陈峰推开“学员宿舍1号”的大门。

    里面四张上下铺铁架床，床板上铺着发霉的褥子。

    靠墙的桌子上摆着几个搪瓷杯，还有一摞书。

    “书？”
content_en:
Entrance to the canteen.

Chen Feng stared at the crooked plaque in the fog, his heartbeat speeding up slightly.

After waiting for so long, I can finally go in and take a look.

He gripped the chopping knife tightly and moved toward the martial arts hall.

He stopped at the door and didn't rush in.

Instead, he bent down to pick up a few pieces of gravel and threw them into the martial arts hall gate.

The stone fell to the ground and bounced a few times, the sound echoing in the empty room.

No response.

He waited for another ten seconds to confirm that there was no movement of other alien creatures inside, and then stepped sideways into the door.

The hall on the first floor of the martial arts hall is very spacious, at least 200 square meters, but it has changed beyond recognition at this time.

The ground was covered with gray-white spider silk remnants, and broken bones and unknown remains were piled in the corners.

Several load-bearing pillars were also wrapped with thick silk threads, stuck together with rags and moldy wooden boards.

The air was filled with a sour smell, mixed with the unique fishy smell of spiders.

This place has been transformed into a nest by the Shadow Hunter Spider.

Chen Feng frowned and carefully stepped on the spider silk and walked inside.

There are still some things left on the wall.

Under the spider silk, you can vaguely see framed photos and text introductions.

Chen Feng used the back of his knife to push aside the covering silk screen, revealing the content underneath.

A yellowed photo of a muscular middle-aged man, shirtless, posing in a strange posture.

The back is curved, the arms are drooping, and the whole person's posture is bent and twisted, not like a human being, but like a fat snake standing upright.

There is a line of small words below the photo:

"The sixty-fourth generation descendant of Snake Ridge Liu Changhe."

"Provincial second-level martial artist, member of Donghai City Martial Arts Association."

There are also large promotional posters posted on several walls nearby.

"Snake spine flow - overcome hardness with softness, overcome clumsiness with skill."

"The Liu Family Martial Arts School was established seventeen years ago and has trained more than 200 disciples."

…

Chen Feng watched as he walked.

The core concept of Snake Spine Ryu is to simulate the movement of snake spines for practice and fighting.

And through special methods and secret medicines, the genetic lock of the human body is gradually opened, thereby achieving a leap-forward improvement in physical fitness.

This information is basically consistent with what was recorded in the diary...

Afterwards, Chen Feng looked around on the first floor, but did not find any Kung Fu books or teaching manuscripts.

Then I went to the owner's office on the second floor and searched in detail.

The cabinets were all open, the drawers were all scattered on the floor, and there was nothing inside.

Most of the remaining scattered yellowed documents are student registration forms and fee records, which are of little use.

"Where's the technique..."

Chen Feng stood up, frowning and looking around.

It stands to reason that in a martial arts gym, the most important thing, such as the secrets and techniques, should be placed in the gym owner's office.

If it doesn’t even exist here, then it most likely means it doesn’t exist elsewhere either…

Chen Feng felt a wave of unwillingness in his heart.

"That's not the case..."

After so much effort, you found nothing?

"I don't believe it."

He walked out of the owner's office and continued walking deeper into the corridor.

The several rooms at the back seemed to be dormitories. The door numbers read "Student Dormitory No. 1", "Student Dormitory No. 2"... all the way to No. 6.

Chen Feng pushed open the door of "Student Dormitory No. 1".

There were four bunk beds with iron frames inside, with moldy mattresses covering the bed boards.

There are several enamel cups on the table against the wall, as well as a stack of books.

"Book?"
